questions.prompt: Which ancient civilization built the Parthenon?
questions.fact: It has almost no straight lines; columns bulge slightly and the base curves, corrections for how the eye perceives scale.

questions.prompt: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.fact: The count dropped by one in 2006 when a new definition required a body to have cleared its orbital neighbourhood.

questions.prompt: In athletics, how many hurdles are in a 110-metre hurdles race?
questions.fact: Elite runners take exactly three strides between each one, which is why the event rewards a very specific stride length.

questions.prompt: Which band is fronted by Mick Jagger?
questions.fact: They were named after a Muddy Waters song, chosen hurriedly during a phone call with a venue asking what to print.

questions.prompt: Which desert covers much of Mongolia and northern China?
questions.fact: It is a cold desert where winter temperatures fall well below freezing and snow sometimes settles on the dunes.

questions.prompt: Which Shakespeare play features the character Shylock?
questions.fact: It was classed as a comedy in the first collected edition, a label modern productions tend to resist.

questions.prompt: Which programming language is known for the phrase 'write once, run anywhere'?
questions.fact: Programs compile to an intermediate bytecode run by a virtual machine, which is what makes the portability claim work.
